dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: ānande mahati prāpte dṛṣṭe vā bāndhave cirāt | ānandam udgataṃ dhyātvā tallayas tanmanā bhavet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: When a great joy is attained, or on seeing a friend or relative after a long time, let one meditate on the joy that has arisen; absorbed in it, the mind becomes one with it.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: on such occasions one should lay hold of the source of the experience, the pure spiritual pulse (spanda), and meditate on it until the mind is steeped in it; because the experience vanishes quickly it should be seized as soon as it occurs. Wallis: meditate on that joy as it slowly disappears; let the mind dissolve into it.
dharana.technique_name: Merging with a Great Joy, Such as Meeting a Friend
dharana.instruction: When great joy arrives, turn from its cause to the joy itself and merge with it.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 71 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the joy itself, attended to directly
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a wave of joy in time: it rises with an occasion, and attention turns from the occasion to the joy itself.
geometry.svg_hint: a rising and falling wave with its crest highlighted
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Turn to the joy itself
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: attention moves from the happy event to the joy itself, and the mind merges with it. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn from the happy event to the feeling of joy itself
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.gaze: Eyes open; this happens in ordinary life
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The joy itself as it arises, rather than its cause
attention.secondary: Staying with it as it fades

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: When a great joy is attained, or on seeing a friend or relative after a long time, let one meditate on the joy that has arisen; absorbed in it, the mind becomes one with it.
adiyogi.method_summary: When a great joy arrives (seeing a friend after a long time, good news), turn attention from the event to the joy itself. Feel it as it rises, stay with it, and let the mind merge with it, also as it fades. Do it at once; such moments pass quickly.

honesty.disclosure: Door 048 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 48 (verse 71) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 048 is dharana 48, verse 71. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).

The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Stay present with the person in front of you; this is a quiet inner turning, not a withdrawal from them. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Attention
